subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should these 14 action updates land as one group after targeted trusted workflow runs, or should the credential- and agent-bearing action families be split for isolated review?
rationale: The source changes are mechanical, but several updated actions execute with repository secrets or alter agent sandbox setup in workflows that normal PR checks cannot fully exercise.

options.title: Validate and merge together
options.body: Refresh the branch, complete exact-head checks, and run representative trusted token, Codex, Docker, and CodeQL workflows before merging the grouped update.

options.title: Split sensitive action families
options.body: Separate GitHub App token, Docker login/release, and Codex action pins so each secret-bearing boundary can be validated and rolled back independently.

options.title: Accept grouped runtime risk
options.body: Merge after ordinary checks without targeted secret-bearing workflow proof, accepting that failures may first appear in scheduled, agent, or release operations.

recommendation.title: Validate and merge together
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch, complete exact-head checks, and run representative trusted token, Codex, Docker, and CodeQL workflows before merging the grouped update.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person most directly to the affected release-workflow validation and Docker publication paths.
